messages:
maya: kicking off a wide sweep of the replay harness against last week's prod traces. purpose: validate new kernel-selector rules + revised batching window + KV warmup tweak. starting small then scale up. will post quick findings here.

sam: thanks — what config are you using for the kernel selector? the PR changed the threshold math (commit 12ab3f).

maya: good q. using `--kernel-policy=latency-weighted-v2` and `--pivot-quantile=0.75`. also toggling `--batch-window-ms` between 5/10/20 to see throughput/latency tradeoffs. command: ```./replay_run --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-10 --anon-salt=redw-03 --sample-rate=0.02 --kernel-policy=latency-weighted-v2 --pivot-quantile=0.75 --batch-window-ms=10```

oliver: perf note — when we shrink batch-window to 5ms we see more kernel switches and metric variance. might exercise kernel-selection race conditions. saw non-deterministic kernel choice on GPUs with mixed-precision fallback before. :eyes:

replay-bot: run summary 2276004338: traces processed 462, overall token delta vs prod baseline 0.87%, failed parity checks 3. auto-attach: /artifacts/run-2276004338/flame.tar.gz

maya: quick breakdown from the first 3k requests:
- pivot=0.75 + batch-window=10ms => stable kernel selection for >90% of short sequences
- batch-window=5ms => 1.6x higher variance in per-request latency, kernel flip on ~0.9% of traces
- KV warmup tweak (prewarm window 50 tokens) reduced cold-hit latency by ~12% but introduced rare divergence when kernel swap occurs mid-warmup

kai: divergence how? is it token-level mismatch or just timing?

maya: token-level deltas. reproduced with smaller trace slice: when we switch kernels between token 16-19, KV cache eviction order differs leading to small token drift starting at token 21. patch hypothesis: KV index rebuild isn't being performed identically across kernels.

anita: that's worrying. can you capture a minimal repro trace and put it in a private bucket? also, is the anonymization pipeline deterministic? different salts could mask true parity.

maya: anonymization deterministic — we use `--anon-salt` seeds and cohort-preserving hashing. confirmed same salt across runs. repro trace uploaded to s3://ci-repro/replay-kv-drift/trace-2276004360.gz (private).

sam: next steps idea: run a two-pass parity check: 1) run emulation with kernel A pinned for whole trace, 2) kernel B pinned, 3) allow selector to switch. compare diffs and dump KV snapshots at switch points.

maya: doing that now. also generating perf profiles (nsight/cpu flame) around the switch events. linking logs: <https://internal-logs/runs/2276004338>

replay-bot: parity job 2276004389 queued (2 pinned kernels vs selector). estimated runtime 45m.

oliver: FYI, earlier kernel changes touched the allocator path — if allocator addresses or ordering differ, KV key iteration order can vary on some kernels. maybe add deterministic sort in the rebuild step as a cheap guard.

maya: good call. will add deterministic sort to KV rebuild and re-run. patch quick diff: ```- for k in kv: rebuild(k) + rebuild_index(k) + maybe_shuffle() + commit ``` ```+ for k in sorted(kv): rebuild(k) + rebuild_index(k) + commit```

sam: also please collect GPU kernel launch timestamps + stream ids. could help correlate asynchronous ops.

maya: collected. initial pinned runs: kernel-A pinned (no switches) => token parity 0.00% vs prod baseline; kernel-B pinned => 0.01% (tiny). selector-run => 0.95% with divergence concentrated in 12 traces. after deterministic-sort patch re-run scheduled.

anita: are we confident sampling isn't biasing these 12 traces? maybe they're from a rare cohort (long-concat sessions). check cohort tags.

maya: checked — 9/12 are long-history sessions (>180 tokens) and same cohort id hash prefix. they hit our KV prewarm path frequently.

replay-bot: run 2276004475 finished: post-patch selector-run token delta 0.08%, failed parity 0. flagged traces reduced from 12 -> 2. artifacts: /artifacts/run-2276004475/diffs.tar.gz

oliver: huge improvement. can you open a follow-up test to stress sequence boundaries (token lengths 150-400) with higher sample weight? I want to confirm no edgecases.

maya: will do a targeted sweep across 150/200/300/400 lengths, increasing sample-rate to 0.1 for those cohorts only. kicking off now. command: ```./replay_run --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-10 --filter-max-tokens 400 --cohort-filter long_hist --sample-rate 0.1 --kernel-policy=latency-weighted-v2 --anon-salt=redw-03```

sam: also file a quick RFC for adding deterministic rebuild as a permanent invariant. we should have unit tests that assert same KV snapshot across kernels given same inputs.

anita: agreed. tagging @security for anonymization audit.

maya: tl;dr: root cause likely non-deterministic KV rebuild ordering exposed when kernel swap happens mid-warmup; short-term fix = deterministic sort on rebuild + extra parity guards; next = add unit tests and kernel-launch tracing. overall perf trade: deterministic sort negligible overhead in rebuild path (microbenchmarked).

sam: great work. can you open a ticket with steps to backport to dedicated runtime? put links to artifacts and the minimal repro. once that's green we can merge the selector change. :thumbsup:

maya: created REDW-8712 with attachments and reproduction notes. linking PR: https://github.com/redwood/replay/pull/1256

oliver: thanks — will review the PR and the perf profiles later today.

maya: ending run now. will post final results here when long-cohort sweep completes. :wave:
